title: climux description document
description: A command tree described by go.hotsrc.dev/climux, at schema version 1. Whitespace and key order are not part of the format: compare parsed values, never bytes. See docs/adr/machine-readable-schema.md for the design this specifies.

schemaVersion.description: Identifies the shape of this document. This schema covers version 1.

command.description: A command users may invoke: its own name, the flags it accepts and every subcommand beneath it. Does not repeat a flag inherited from an ancestor. May gain further properties in a later document at this schema version.

name.description: The command's own name, unqualified by its ancestry: "add" rather than "orbital remote add".

fullName.description: Name joined with each ancestor's, from the root down: "orbital remote add".

hidden.description: The command is omitted from help output.

forwardArgs.description: Arguments following a "--" terminator are passed through to the command rather than rejected.

forwarded.description: Names the arguments the command hands to its handler unparsed: what follows an interrupt command's name, or a ForwardArgs command's -- terminator. Absent when the program named nothing, which does not say nothing is forwarded.

valueName.description: How the forwarded arguments are shown where the command's arguments are, already written for a reader.

flagGroup.description: A nominal grouping of flags, which affects how the flags are shown in help messages. May gain further properties in a later document at this schema version.

flag.description: A command line flag or positional argument: what it is called, what options reach it, and what kind of value it takes. May gain further properties in a later document at this schema version.

name.description: The flag's declared canonical name, undecorated by any dialect: "force" rather than "--force". A positional argument's name is the name it was declared with, same as any other flag.

valueName.description: How the value the flag takes is written where the flag is shown to a reader, such as the "SERVICE" of "Usage: deploy SERVICE". A positional argument, which names no option, is shown by this alone.

kind.description: The kind of value the flag takes. Absent for an interrupt, which binds no value and so has none to classify. A duration is written in Go's duration syntax: a decimal number with a unit suffix, such as 30s, 250ms or 1h30m.

default.description: The flag's default value, already rendered as a string.

showDefault.description: A formatter should print default beside usage.

positional.description: The flag is an operand rather than an option: named by position on the command line rather than by any of options.

hidden.description: The flag is omitted from help output.

maxCount.description: The most times the flag may be given, or 0 for no limit.

envVar.description: The name of the environment variable that supplies the flag's value when it is not given on the command line. The variable's own value never appears here.

choices.description: The only values the flag accepts, or absent when any value is accepted.

takesValue.description: Naming the flag on the command line consumes a value. A boolean flag omits this: naming it alone stands for true.

options.description: Every option that reaches the flag: the canonical name's option, then the short name's, then any further aliases, then every option a dialect generated, in that order. A positional argument has none.

option.description: One spelling a flag answers to on the command line, and what naming it that way means for the value. May gain further properties in a later document at this schema version.
The option as a reader would type it: "--force" or "-f".

effect.description: What typing this option does to the flag's value, such as "negate". The vocabulary is open and grows over time: a consumer that meets an effect it does not recognize must not offer that option, having no way to know what typing it does. Absent means the ordinary case: naming the flag this way sets it.
